To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

limited angle tomography of the vasculature can be improved by incorporating a priori information of the object density distributions and that the best reconstruction performance is achieved using an algorithm based on the maximum a priori probability (MAP) principle.

limited angle tomography can provide high resolution images of blood vessels, with the resolution determined by the number of projections, the angular range of the projections, the field of view, and the size of the object.

the best reconstruction performance is achieved by combining two pieces of a-priori knowledge: (1) The object is dilute; (2) The density distribution is non-negative; and (3) The amount of residual blur can be significantly reduced without a significant penalty in diminished SNRs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an algorithm for reconstructing blood vessel distributions from a limited number x-ray projections.
the development of an algorithm that can be used to reconstruct blood vessels from a small number of x-ray projections, distributed over only a limited angle.
the development of a new algorithm for reconstructing blood vessel images from limited angle x-ray subtraction projections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a given SNR, tomosynthetic reconstructions are superior to filtered backprojection reconstructions, but that the latter can be improved by incorporating a priori information about the vascular density distributions.
the use of a priori vascular knowledge in a reconstruction algorithm can improve the image quality in terms of both SNR and out-of-focus blur.
the best results were obtained using the limited angle algorithm with the two pieces of a-priori knowledge incorporated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
limited-angle tomographic reconstruction is feasible and can produce useful images.
, for limited angle geometry, a priori knowledge can be used to reduce the residual blur in the reconstruction, and that the SNR can be improved by using a more appropriate noise model.
the best reconstruction performance is achieved when the object is diluted and when non-negative density constraints are imposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
limited angle reconstruction can be performed using a priori knowledge about the object.

the limited-angle geometry can be used to reconstruct blood vessel distributions from a few x-ray projections, provided that the vessel density is dilute and the reconstruction algorithm is designed with this in mind.
the use of a priori information about the expected object can be a very effective way to reduce the effects of limited angle data.
